sections.heading: Staying Compliant: Opt-Ins, Quality Rating and Message Templates

blocks.html: A live account only stays healthy if you play by Meta's rules from the first send. These four habits protect your number and keep your delivery strong.

items.title: Collect explicit opt-ins:
items.desc: Only message people who have clearly agreed to hear from you — a consent checkbox at signup or checkout is the safest route.

items.title: Watch your quality rating:
items.desc: Meta grades each number green, yellow or red based on how customers react. Staying green keeps your limits climbing.

items.title: Master message templates:
items.desc: Outbound marketing and utility messages must use pre-approved templates in the correct category — miscategorising them risks rejection.

items.title: Respect messaging tiers:
items.desc: New numbers begin at a lower daily limit and expand as you send consistently to opted-in users with good quality.

sections.heading: Fixing the Most Common Onboarding Problems

blocks.html: Almost every hold-up falls into one of these buckets. Here's what each one means and how to clear it fast.

items.title: Display name rejected:
items.desc: If your WhatsApp Business API display name is rejected, align it exactly with your website and legal brand, drop any promotional wording, and resubmit — most pass on the second try.

items.title: Business verification failed:
items.desc: This almost always means a mismatch — the name or address on your documents does not match your Business Manager. Fix the detail and re-submit.

items.title: Stuck at a low messaging limit:
items.desc: Warm the number up gradually and keep quality green — the WhatsApp Business API messaging limits rise on their own as trust builds.

items.title: Review taking too long:
items.desc: Usually a pending piece of Business Manager information. Complete every requested field and the queue clears.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions: Getting Started on the Platform

items.q: What is the WhatsApp Business API and how is it set up?
items.a: The WhatsApp Business API is a Meta-verified messaging layer for medium and large businesses, with no chat app of its own. It's set up through an official Meta Business Solution Provider (BSP) like Ojiva AI, which connects your number to automation, a shared inbox and your business systems, and handles Meta verification, display-name approval and template review on your behalf.

items.q: How long does WhatsApp Business API verification take?
items.a: Once your documents are in order, Meta usually reviews a display name within about a day, though business verification can take longer if details need re-checking. A partner that pre-checks your information before submission helps avoid the back-and-forth that causes most delays.

items.q: Can I use my existing phone number for the setup?
items.a: Yes, but a number can run on either the free Business App or the API, not both at once. If the number is already active in the app, it must be removed there first, so many businesses plan the switch carefully or start onboarding on a fresh number.

items.q: Do I need DLT registration for the WhatsApp Business API?
items.a: No. DLT registration applies to SMS in India. WhatsApp relies on Meta's own business verification, display-name approval and message-template review instead. If you also send SMS, that separate channel still needs DLT — see our DLT registration guide.

items.q: Why was my display name rejected and how do I fix it?
items.a: A display name is usually rejected when it doesn't clearly match your real brand or the branding on your website. Align the name exactly with your website and legal entity, remove generic or promotional wording, and resubmit — most names pass on the second attempt once they match.

items.q: Is there a licence fee for the WhatsApp Business API?
items.a: There's no software licence fee for API access. You pay Meta per conversation by category, plus your provider's platform fee, with 18% GST on top. Replies inside the 24-hour customer service window are not charged, so most support conversations cost nothing extra.

items.q: What is a WABA and do I need a Meta Business Manager?
items.a: A WABA is your WhatsApp Business Account — the container that holds your number, display name and templates. Yes, you need a Meta Business Manager with admin access, because that's where your business is verified and your WABA lives.

items.q: How do I increase my WhatsApp messaging limit?
items.a: New numbers start at a lower messaging tier and expand as you send consistently to opted-in users while keeping your quality rating green. Warming the number up gradually, sending relevant template messages and avoiding blocks and reports is what moves you up the tiers.
